module.adapter: Vendor elements, events, focus trapping and --wa-* variables remain replaceable inside the implementation.

contract.evidence: User explicitly approved the ten Dialog judgments and the deterministic 32-instance Legacy mapping after reviewing the complete rules in conversation.

sizeMigration.note: The approved wide trial becomes Large; the former viewport-sized Large becomes X-Large.

judgments: Dialog is a modal interruption for one bounded task or focused inspection that cannot remain safely in the underlying flow; ordinary disclosure, Tooltip, Popover, Menu and page navigation are not Dialogs.
Confirmation Dialog is a narrow specialization for one consequential commit; it does not host forms, previews, multi-step work or general information.

Size describes content capacity rather than importance: small for a short decision, medium for a standard form or focused task, large for a spacious media or split-pane task, and x-large for a viewport-sized, high-density modal workspace.

Every Dialog has one accessible title, one body region and an optional footer action row; a visually hidden title is allowed only when visible media or domain content already supplies the visual heading.

Ordinary Dialogs expose zero or one primary action and optional secondary/quiet actions; Confirmation Dialogs expose exactly Cancel and Confirm, with destructive tone only when the consequence is destructive.
Explicit dismissal is the default and the only policy for forms, unsaved state and all Confirmation Dialogs; light dismissal is reserved for read-only, lossless inspection.
Focus enters deterministically, remains contained while modal, closes on Escape unless a non-interruptible commit is in progress, and returns to the invoker when possible.
Nested Dialogs are prohibited; a task that needs another modal step must replace or sequence the current Dialog.
Immersive editing Dialogs may customize the modal backdrop only through --ic-dialog-backdrop-color and --ic-dialog-backdrop-filter; callers must not consume Vendor backdrop variables directly.
Immersive presentation is reserved for x-large, explicitly dismissed editing workspaces; its viewport sizing remains owned by ic-dialog and Confirmation Dialogs cannot use it.
Compact Modal presentation reuses the small Dialog shell at a 32rem preferred width with restrained header, body and footer spacing; it is a reusable task composition, not a fifth Dialog size.
A subtitle title structure is supplied through slot=label so the Dialog-owned native h2 remains the only heading level-two element; callers never nest another h2 inside the label.
The medium-explicit-task footer pattern names action density and order rather than Dialog width: a visible secondary text action precedes one visible primary text action, with no decorative arrow.
Dialog and Confirmation Dialog share one interruptible modal motion lifecycle; callers own task meaning and content, not duplicated surface or Backdrop animation.

small.purpose: Short decision, compact message or narrow single-purpose task.

medium.purpose: Default form, settings or focused task.

large.purpose: Spacious media, split-pane inspection or editing without becoming a viewport-sized workspace.

x-large.purpose: High-density libraries, inspection or editing presented as one viewport-sized modal workspace.

sizes.narrowViewport: Small, medium and large fit the viewport with central spacing Tokens. X-Large occupies 90% of the viewport width and 92% of the viewport height; body content scrolls before header or footer actions leave view.

header: optional close action when dismissal is available
contentStructure.body: Owns task content and the only vertical scroll region.
contentStructure.footer: Optional for ic-dialog; required for ic-confirmation-dialog.

labelStructures.slot: label attribute or slot=label plain text

labelStructures.markupRule: Use non-heading descendants for title and subtitle; nested h2 is prohibited.

motion.entry: Fade and move the standard surface from one --ui-space-2 step below while scaling from .96 to 1, using --ui-motion-duration-release and --ui-motion-ease-fluid. Fade the Backdrop in with --ui-motion-duration-normal and --ui-motion-ease-standard, transitioning its filter from no blur to the default 2px blur.
motion.exit: Reverse the surface and Backdrop relationship with --ui-motion-duration-fast and --ui-motion-ease-press. Keep the native Dialog open until the visual exit settles, then close it, return focus and emit ic-after-hide.
motion.interruption: Reopening during exit cancels stale close completion and re-enters the same modal task without emitting an obsolete ic-after-hide event.
motion.immersive: Immersive Dialogs retain fade and Backdrop continuity but remove surface translation and scale.
motion.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion and data-ui-motion=reduced keep the state lifecycle but remove translation and scale and reduce durations to 1ms through central Tokens.

initialFocusOrder: Dialog surface as a programmatic focus fallback
focusManagement.confirmationInitialFocus: Cancel receives initial focus by default; an explicit non-destructive Confirm may opt in to initial focus.
focusManagement.containment: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the topmost open Dialog.
focusManagement.returnFocus: return to the invoking element when it remains connected and focusable
focusManagement.fallbackReturn: otherwise focus the nearest connected focusable ancestor, then the document's main landmark
focusManagement.focusVisible: Keyboard focus uses the confirmed central --ui-* Focus interface; pointer focus does not fabricate a visible ring.

components.purpose: Present one labeled modal task or focused inspection with project-owned structure, dismissal and focus management.
useWhen: The underlying flow must be temporarily unavailable.
The content is one bounded task, form or focused inspection.
invariants: Header and footer remain visible while an overflowing body scrolls.
compact requires size=small and defaults to a 32rem preferred inline size.
Invalid combinations fail closed and emit ic-contract-error.

components.purpose: Require an explicit Cancel or Confirm choice immediately before one consequential action commits.
useWhen: The consequence is costly, difficult to reverse or destructive.
The user still has a meaningful opportunity to cancel.

actionLayout.narrowViewport: stack only when translated labels cannot fit without truncation; Confirm remains last in DOM and visual order

invariants: Cancel and Confirm are always visibly labeled.
Backdrop activation never closes the Dialog.
Escape is equivalent to Cancel unless confirm-loading is active.
confirm-loading prevents duplicate commit and dismissal until the current commit settles.

runtimeContract.engineBoundary: Business and acceptance sources consume only ic-* tags, native platform/ARIA behavior and central --ui-* Tokens.
runtimeContract.tracerCompatibility: The initial tracer label, open, light-dismiss, without-header, show/hide events and focus entry/return evidence remain technical feasibility only; the Dialog interface supersedes tracer naming where this contract differs.

legacyCoverage.rule: Legacy evidence proves coverage and product demand; it does not define target sizes, structure, dismissal or appearance.
